docs.title: Extend the graphical interface
docs.text:
Open Knowledge Architecture.canvas from this folder in Obsidian. Drag notes from the file explorer into the Canvas; resize and group cards; label connections with their relation type. Add your own diagrams or images to this folder and embed them in notes. Describe what each visual asserts and its source. Canvas edges do not automatically update the typed relations in Markdown: reconcile them during review.

The SVG is a separate editable overview, not a live projection of the Canvas. Published readers can use this note's map and links without depending on a Canvas renderer. Canvas rendering on the target Publish site remains untested.

docs.title: Neurosemantic knowledge core
docs.text:
Finocchio presents knowledge as entities, relations, states, rules, decisions and evidence. Narrative and explanation complement a symbolic layer for identity, typing, provenance and constraints. Documents become views of this knowledge. This is an architectural proposition in the presentation, not empirical proof of effectiveness.

Implementation: both thematic portals link to one canonical set of notes. English paraphrases, typed links and source locators are stored together. This prototype does not run an LLM, inference engine or graph database.

docs.title: Ontology and entity relations
docs.text:
Use stable identifiers, never names alone. Entity classes: Concept, Claim, SourceVersion, EvidenceArtifact, AIUseCase, Organization, HumanRole, Risk, Control, Decision and ReviewEvent. A report of a result is distinct from the result itself.

Relations have direction and scope: Claim supportedBy SourceVersion; Claim contradictedBy EvidenceArtifact; AIUseCase exposesTo Risk; Control mitigates Risk; Decision authorizedBy HumanRole; Entry derivedFrom SourceVersion; SourceVersion supersedes SourceVersion. A thematic classification is a view membership, not a duplicate entity.

Domain/range checks prevent a Control from authorizing a Decision. Source relevance, authority and truth require additional review. RDF/OWL, SKOS, gUFO and PROV-O are mentioned on slide 7; their complete formal integration is future work.

docs.title: Provenance and evidence custody
docs.text:
The presentation distinguishes traces of events, attributed reports and authoritative references, and stresses origin, version, applicability and custody. These categories are not interchangeable evidence grades.

Implementation custody protocol: register original bytes without alteration; calculate SHA-256; record acquisition time, custodian, access scope and rights; create separately identified extraction/translation derivatives; link each claim to a source version and precise locator; retain contradictions and superseded revisions. A hash supports integrity comparison, not authorship or truth.

An operational custody ledger must record actor, timestamp, input/output hashes, action, reason and authorization. This local package fingerprints the supplied PDF but does not distribute it, retain its personal watermark or implement a tamper-proof custody service.

docs.title: Semantic and epistemic validation
docs.text:
Finocchio distinguishes plausibility, coherence and truth. Semantic checking asks whether types and relations make sense; epistemic checking asks how a claim is supported. Passing a structural constraint does not establish truth.

Implementation checks: unique IDs, valid endpoints and allowed relation types; provenance fields; unknown source records; review status and accountable owner. Human epistemic review then examines source reliability, contradictory evidence, context, applicability and whether conclusions exceed the evidence. Do not promote expected benefits into observed results or infer causality from correlation.

The earlier HTML prototype includes a limited JavaScript lint. This Obsidian edition provides review notes and editable model files; it does not execute that lint or a SHACL engine.

docs.title: Human-in-command jurisdiction
docs.text:
The slide assigns bounded jurisdiction to agents and human authorization to consequential action; absence, ambiguity and conflict trigger escalation.

Implementation rule: AI may suggest, summarize, classify and flag conflicts. Only a named human acting within a recorded scope may accept an interpretation, change an authoritative entry or authorize action. A rule evaluation is advice unless explicitly delegated within that scope. Missing permission never becomes permission.

Approval record: actor identity, role, scope, affected revision hash, evidence reviewed, rationale, conditions, time and expiry. Material changes invalidate earlier approval. Emergency restrictions may suspend use pending review. This prototype has no authenticated roles and therefore offers no approval or execution button.

docs.title: Version-aware answers and human escalation
docs.text:
Require an answer to cite an approved source version with effective date and applicability scope. When sources conflict or permission is unclear, withhold an authoritative answer and route the case to the responsible human.

Test with missing, obsolete and contradictory sources. Keep test inputs, expected behavior, actual behavior and reviewer decisions. Measure failures rather than declaring the control effective by design. Implementation and effectiveness: not demonstrated. This control is an original proposal, not a verbatim NIST requirement.

docs.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0 — pinned reference
docs.text:
Pinned edition: NIST AI 100-1, AI RMF 1.0, January 2023. Its core organizes work into GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE, with governance crossing the other functions. The framework is voluntary.

Proposed local mapping: record authority and ownership; describe context and affected people; evaluate evidence; track treatment decisions. This mapping is editorial and does not constitute certification or a NIST endorsement.

Checked 31 October 2026: the official landing page states that 1.0 is being revised. Retain this version; add a distinct SourceVersion for a replacement and assess changed mappings before adoption. The Playbook and Generative AI Profile are separate references, not silently merged into 1.0.

docs.title: Citizen-service assistant: a bounded use case
docs.text:
A hypothetical agency considers an assistant to explain published service requirements. Intended benefit: easier access to information. Observed benefit: unknown; no deployment or evaluation data are supplied.

Boundary: cite the applicable publication and effective date, expose uncertainty and route contested or personal cases to a human. The assistant cannot determine eligibility, issue a binding decision or modify a citizen record.

Evidence plan: test answer fidelity, accessibility, language coverage, omission rates and escalation quality using a documented sample. Compare to a baseline; record costs and adverse outcomes. Record who can approve a pilot and whose rights may be affected. Local legal applicability remains unassessed.

docs.title: Public value and accountability
docs.text:
Separate outputs (answers delivered), outcomes (users completing a process), impacts (wider institutional effects) and causal attribution. Efficiency claims need denominators, a baseline, measurement period and cost assumptions.

Record service owner, affected groups, public-interest objective, accessibility requirements, complaint route and review authority. A vendor assertion is a report until independently examined. A framework reference does not establish legal compliance. This entry proposes a research and governance structure; it reports no achieved public benefit.

docs.title: Unsupported authoritative answers
docs.text:
An assistant may state an outdated or unsupported service condition with unwarranted confidence. Possible consequences include exclusion, wasted time and loss of trust. These are plausible risks in this hypothetical case, not observed incidents. Likelihood, severity and residual risk are unknown.

Assessment must identify affected people, exposure, evidence, uncertainty, existing safeguards, accountable risk owner and review trigger. Escalate conflicting references; do not choose whichever source ranks highest in retrieval.

Filename suggests 30 October 2026; slide 3 separately bears August 2026. Do not treat these as a resolved publication date.

Source map: pp. 5–7 graph projections and dual layers; pp. 10–11 ontology and distinct validation lenses; pp. 12–13 provenance and custody; p. 14 ontology/process/decision/case integration; p. 17 state and validated handoffs; p. 18 agent jurisdiction; p. 19 four architectural layers. These are paraphrases of extractable text, not independent validation of the claims.

Pages 3, 8, 9, 15 and 16 have little or no substantive extractable text; visual content was not inspected. The two portals, entity schema, UI, workflow implementation, NIST mapping and fictional examples are proposed here, not attributed to the author. The source contains a reproduction restriction. No slide images, full text or PDF are redistributed.

docs.title: Editorial workflow and review gates
docs.text:
1. Intake: register source, rights, confidentiality, version and custody.
  2. Extract: preserve original; isolate OCR and translation derivatives with page locators.
  3. Model: create typed entities, claims and scoped relations; mark uncertainty.
  4. Validate: run structural checks, then semantic and epistemic human review.
  5. Authorize: designated human signs a fixed revision within jurisdiction; unresolved conflicts block approval.
  6. Release: publish only after separate publication authorization; both views should use the same approved revision.
  7. Monitor: review expiry, source changes, complaints and counterevidence; withdraw or supersede without erasing history.

Roles: contributor proposes; knowledge steward maintains identity and provenance; subject reviewer assesses meaning and evidence; accountable authority approves within scope; publisher releases. Roles and separation of duties must be assigned before production. All supplied entries remain drafts.

docs.text:
The conceptual starting point is José Finocchio Junior's supplied 23-page presentation, Engenharia do Conhecimento para Equipes e Projetos: Do paradigma documental ao sistema neurosemântico. Page locators identify the basis of English paraphrases. The ontology schema, thematic portals, examples, Obsidian organization and workflow are proposed adaptations, not assertions of the author's endorsement. Consult the source register for date ambiguity and custody details.

The original PDF, slide images, full transcription and personal watermark are excluded. The original includes a reproduction restriction. The source was text-extracted; image-only content was not visually reviewed. Publication rights for further source-derived materials must be assessed before adding them.

NIST references are versioned external sources. Mention does not imply certification, endorsement or legal compliance.

docs.title: How to contribute
docs.text:
1. Create a note from the local Knowledge Entry template in 06 Templates. Keep it unpublished while drafting.
  2. Give it a unique ID, entity type and explicit attribution category. Separate source paraphrase from your interpretation.
  3. Record the exact source version, locator, applicability and contrary evidence. Missing evidence remains unknown.
  4. Add labeled relations to existing canonical notes; link it from one or both portals.
  5. Request semantic and epistemic review. Record the reviewer, date, revision, decision and rationale.
  6. The accountable human decides acceptance and release scope. Preserve prior versions separately before material edits.

Reading access on Publish does not by itself grant vault editing. Collaboration arrangements and permissions remain to be chosen. Do not email a shared vault password as part of an automated release.
